items.followUp: Define boiling point and explain how it is related to the vapour pressure of a liquid.

rubric.why: Credits the definition and its essential equilibrium condition.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.how: Mention the vapour, the liquid, and equilibrium.

rubric.why: Checks the effect of temperature on vapour pressure.
rubric.description: States that vapour pressure increases when temperature increases.
rubric.how: Give the direction of change as temperature rises.

rubric.why: Checks how the nature of the liquid affects vapour pressure.
rubric.description: States that stronger intermolecular forces result in lower vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Relate stronger forces to fewer molecules escaping into the vapour.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour above its liquid in a closed container when the liquid and vapour are in equilibrium.
Vapour pressure increases when temperature increases because more liquid molecules have enough energy to escape into the vapour.
Vapour pressure also depends on the nature of the liquid: stronger intermolecular forces hold molecules in the liquid more strongly and result in lower vapour pressure.

items.followUp: Differentiate between ionic and covalent compounds, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature and an example of an ionic compound.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds form by electron transfer, producing ions, and gives sodium chloride as an example.
rubric.how: Name electron transfer or ion formation and give a valid ionic example.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature and an example of a covalent compound.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds form when atoms share electrons and gives water as an example.
rubric.how: Name electron sharing and give a valid covalent example.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are formed by transfer of electrons, producing oppositely charged ions; for example, sodium chloride (NaCl).
Covalent compounds are formed when atoms share electrons; for example, water (H₂O).
